newsitem.title: CHINA: BANK OF CHINA IN 230 MLN MARK LOAN TO HANDAN STEEL.
newsitem.headline: BANK OF CHINA IN 230 MLN MARK LOAN TO HANDAN STEEL.

text.p: The Bank of China has obtained a 230 million mark international syndicated loan to be used by a steel firm to import plant, the China Daily said on Wednesday.

The loan, consisting of 85 percent export buyers' credit and 15 percent commercial loans, was signed on Tuesday in Beijing with banks including Barclays Bank Plc, Bayerische Landesbank Girozentrale, IKB Deutsche Industriebank AG and Societe Generale, it said.
The loan would be used by Handan Iron and Steel (Group) Co Ltd, China's 11th biggest producer, to import thin plate continuous casting equipment from Germany, it said.
Construction of the thin plate casting project would cost Handan a total of 3.6 billion yuan, it said.

The export credit has a 13-year term with an annual interest rate at Frankfurt Interbank Offered Rate (FIBOR) plus 0.2 percentage points. The annual interest on the eight-year commercial loans was 0.4 percentage points above FIBOR, it said.
Handan Steel, based in northern Hebei province, posted net profit of 242 million yuan ($29.2 million) in the first half of 1997, second only to Shanghai's Baoshan Iron and Steel Co.
Handan's new thin plate project would be completed in four years, with an output of one million tonnes of plate a year for use in automobiles, refrigerators and washing machines, the newspaper said.
